chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

The Muhrim (one in Ihram), if he kills game, is upon him its compensation (Jaza'), and he gives the game as charity to a poor person. If he returns and kills another game, there is no Jaza' upon him, and Allah takes retribution from him, and the retribution is in the Hereafter. This does not contradict what we have presented from the narrations, because the aspect of it is that we carry it upon the one from whom killing game repeats via the path of intentionality (Al-'Amad). For if the matter is so, the expiation (Kaffarah) is obligatory upon him in the first time, and nothing is obligatory upon him in the second time, and he is among those from whom Allah takes retribution. And if that is upon the mode of inadvertence (Al-Sahw) and forgetfulness (An-Nisyan), the expiation is obligatory upon him every time it repeats from him. This indicates this distinction.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in compensation for a Muhrim who kills game intentionally versus unintentionally?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction in this hadith by distinguishing between intentional recurrence, which incurs only divine retribution (al-Naqima) after the initial compensation, and inadvertent recurrence, which requires repeated compensation. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the role of intent (al-'amd) in determining the nature of the penalty for pilgrims. The ruling underscores the spiritual gravity of violating Ihram restrictions while providing practical legal clarity for repeated offenses.
